transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom / Recording available
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Marisol Reyes (VoltBank CISO), Ben O'Neill (VoltBank Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (VoltBank Compliance)
Links mentioned: security packet (https://redwood.dev/sec/soc2-packet), sample export doc (drive link shared in chat)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros? I'll kick it off, Samir Patel, AE. Leah is our SE, she'll handle the technical flow and demo bits.
[00:18] Marisol: Marisol Reyes, CISO at VoltBank. We've got Ben and Aisha with me. We're mostly focused on auditables — retention and exports for regulator requests.
[00:30] Leah: Hi all, Leah Chen. I'll jump into event types and export mechanics. Apologies in advance if I mis-pronounce anything, I'm recovering from a cold so audio may be fuzzy.
[00:43] Ben: Ben O'Neill here. Platform team. We run Splunk + some Kafka streams for audit ingestion.
[00:50] Aisha: Aisha Khan, compliance lead. Primary ask: bank regulators want verifiable admin trails and proof of key rotation. We also need to map retention to regs — could be up to seven years for some artifacts.

[01:05] Samir: Great. High level: Redwood captures two broad categories of events: admin/control-plane events (user logins, role changes, RBAC admin actions, token issuance, model pin/rollouts) and data-plane events (API requests, payload metadata, embeddings generation events). We call them admin events vs request events for shorthand.
[01:32] Marisol: When you say request events, is the payload logged? We cannot persist PII. Bank data in prompts is sensitive.
[01:42] Leah: Good point. By default Redwood's hosted mode never stores customer prompt content long-term in plaintext. Request-level metadata is logged — request id, model, prompt hash, token counts, latencies, and decision flags. Full request bodies are not retained unless customer turns on retention for debugging, and in those cases we can support redaction or tokenization. Also we have configurable redaction pipelines.
[02:08] Ben: So for proof-of-action we need: who did X, when, from where, and optionally the input hash. Is that captured?
[02:16] Leah: Yes. Admin events include actor (email/service account), IP, timestamp, action type (e.g. role.update, key.rotate, model.deploy), and request IDs that link to request traces. We produce structured JSON events that include a request_id field you can stitch into your SIEM.

[02:40] Marisol: Storage — what retention defaults do you have, and can we set per-event retention? Regulator says some actions require seven year retention.
[02:50] Samir: Default for hosted customers is 90 days for full-text telemetry, 365 for higher-level metrics. But enterprise customers can configure retention per event type. We support retention ranges from 30 days up to multi-year (we've done 7-year retention for banks in private deployments). For hosted customers we typically move older events to cold storage; for private deployments you control the backing store.

[03:12] Aisha: How do we export? Our compliance stack prefers streamed syslog or S3 dumps that our Splunk ingest picks up.
[03:20] Leah: Export options: 1) Continuous streaming via syslog/CEF to your SIEM or relay, 2) S3 bucket deliveries (daily/hourly) with versioned files, 3) Kafka/HTTP webhooks for event-forwarding, 4) BigQuery / GCS export for analytics. Formats are JSON by default, CEF available on request. We also support signed delivery (message-level HMAC) for tamper-evidence.

[03:52] Ben: And delivery security — can we push to a private VPC endpoint or must it go over internet?
[04:00] Leah: For Redwood Private we can deliver directly into your VPC over private peering or private connectors. For hosted we support encrypted push to S3 with VPC endpoints and presigned or cross-account roles. There are options for direct SCP to your storage depending on provider.

[04:20] Marisol: KMS — critical. We cannot have Redwood manage keys for long-term archives. Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM?
[04:29] Leah: Yes. We support BYOK with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we support envelope encryption where your CMK wraps the data key; Redwood never stores the unwrapped customer key. Rotations are supported and we log key-rotation events in the audit trail.

[04:50] Aisha: How granular are KMS logs — do we get evidence of decrypt requests and key usage? Regulators often ask for key access logs.
[04:59] Leah: We capture KMS operation events we initiate (e.g., data key encrypt/decrypt calls) and surface them as admin events. For BYOK the canonical source of truth is your cloud KMS audit logs — Redwood can push a reference link and correlate. If you want us to push those KMS usage metrics into your SIEM, we can bridge that as part of the export pipeline.

[05:25] Samir: One nuance: we separate 'admin audit' from 'user request content'. Admin events are always kept with integrity guarantees and can be immutable-mounted to cold storage. For data privacy you can opt to hash or redact prompt content but still retain a cryptographic fingerprint for traceability.

[05:46] Ben: Can we sign the audit files? We have a compliance rule requiring tamper-proofing of audit archives.
[05:53] Leah: Yes, we can produce signed manifests and per-file signatures with your CMK. Also support append-only object stores with object-lock. For more strict needs we provide a proof-of-seal process: each daily bundle has a manifest signed by a service key; if using CMK we can have the manifest wrapped by your key.

[06:20] Marisol: Are there APIs to pull events ad-hoc for eDiscovery? We may need to provide packet to regulator on short notice.
[06:27] Leah: We expose an audit API that can query by request_id, actor, timeframe, or event type. For large-scale exports, we recommend configuring S3 export or streaming to your SIEM. Ad-hoc exports can be done through the console or API and will be provided as gzipped JSON bundles.

[06:45] Aisha: Retention deletion proofs — do you provide attestations when data is purged?
[06:51] Leah: We emit deletion events in the audit trail that include the retention policy applied and a deletion_manifest. We can also produce an attestation document, signed, that says a set of objects were removed at X time. For some customers we run a quarterly attestation process.

[07:10] Ben: What about role-based access control — who can read the audit logs in your console? We need separation of duties.
[07:16] Samir: Redwood RBAC allows you to define roles with least privilege. By default only admin+audit roles can view raw audit export content. You can restrict access by SSO groups (SAML/SCIM), and add approvals for large exports. All console access is itself an auditable event.

[07:38] Marisol: Audit of auditors — meta. If someone from Redwood Support accesses an export during troubleshooting, is that surfaced?
[07:45] Leah: Yes, support accesses generate support-access events: who, when, what was accessed, justifying ticket id. We also support temporary access tokens with automatic expiry and full recording.

[08:02] Aisha: Data residency — do logs ever leave the region? For EU customers logs need to stay in eu-central-1.
[08:08] Leah: You pick region for export. Hosted customers can request region-bound exports; for enterprise/private we deploy the export pipeline inside your region. We avoid cross-region transfers unless you opt in.

[08:26] Ben: How about performance impact — streaming all request metadata could add latency.
[08:31] Leah: We architected exports to be async; audit generation is non-blocking for request latency. The only latency-sensitive part is synchronous KMS encrypt/decrypt for data plane if you choose envelope encryption with on-request unwrap — there is a small crypto overhead but we measure it. We can cache data keys and reduce KMS calls if allowed by your policy.

[08:56] Marisol: Can you show an example event?
[09:00] Leah: Sure, I'll paste a short sample event in the chat but verbally: event_type: admin.role.change, actor: marisol@voltbank.com, timestamp, source_ip, request_id, affected_resource: service-account/ingest, before and after. For data-plane: event_type: request.generated, request_id, model: redwood-open-1, tokens_in, tokens_out, prompt_hash.
[09:22] Ben: When you say prompt_hash, is it SHA256?
[09:25] Leah: We default to SHA256 but can switch hashes per your ops. If you require HMACed hashes with a shared secret we can do that too.

[09:40] Samir: A common ask is retention tiers and cost. For example, 90-day hot retention for analysis, 1-3 year warm, and 7-year cold archive. Cost scales by hot row-hours and storage. We'll include an example spreadsheet in the packet.

[10:00] Marisol: Logging volume — any guidance for estimates? We need to budget for Splunk ingest.
[10:07] Leah: We typically estimate based on request volume and admin change rate. For a model-heavy app, telemetry can be X KB per request; admin events are small but frequent during rollouts. We'll run a quick sample off your traffic profile after you share QPS estimates.

[10:28] Aisha: How do you handle PII in logs if we accidentally send it in prompts?
[10:33] Leah: We have a redact-first pipeline: detectors for SSNs, account numbers, and PII patterns that can be removed or tokenized before export. You can also configure a controlled debug window where raw content is stored for N days for troubleshooting, then purged.

[10:55] Ben: Is there an immutable chain for events? We want tamper detection.
[11:00] Leah: Two options: 1) Signed manifests + object-lock in storage, 2) append-only ledger that emits Merkle proofs on each bundle. We've implemented Merkle-based auditing for a few regulated customers. That is available in Private or for Hosted with an enterprise contract.

[11:28] Marisol: On SSO — we need SAML + SCIM provisioning and group mapping into RBAC. How do you map groups into roles?
[11:36] Samir: We support SAML and SCIM. SCIM handles provisioning and group sync; you map identity groups to Redwood roles in the console. We also support provisioning-only flows if you want to manage access centrally.

[11:52] Aisha: For regulators we need a runbook: how to extract specific audit slices on demand and provide them. Can you commit to a 48-hour turnaround?

[11:58] Samir: Yes, for enterprise customers we commit and SLA that includes expeditious exports for regulatory requests. We will align on SLA language in the contract.

[12:10] Ben: A few small things: what about log schema versioning? If you upgrade event schema will that break our ingestion?
[12:18] Leah: We version event schemas and publish changelogs. Backwards compatibility is a priority; we maintain stable fields and add new ones as optional. If we do a breaking change we'll provide a migration window.

[12:36] Marisol: Would you be able to provide sample signed export from a staging tenant so we can validate ingest into Splunk?
[12:42] Samir: Absolutely, that's one of the next steps. We'll send S3 sample + syslog stream.

[12:50] Leah: Quick note — some words in the transcript may be off, auto-transcript tends to mislabel KMS as K-M-S and KV cache as K-V cash; ignore that.

[13:02] Marisol: Haha noted.

[13:08] Samir: To recap: Redwood captures admin and request events, supports configurable retention up to multi-year, exports via S3/syslog/Kafka/BigQuery, supports BYOK/KMS/HSM, provides signed manifests and tamper-evidence, and has RBAC + SAML/SCIM integration. We'll share SOC 2 notes and a sample export and schedule a short demo stream.

[13:36] Aisha: Sounds good. If you can include the event schema doc and example Splunk ingest config that would be super-helpful.

[13:44] Samir: Noted. Leah, any closing technical caveats?

[13:49] Leah: Only that if you need synchronous decryption with per-request KMS checks we may see a small latency bump; we can tune with caching if regulator policy allows. Also we'll provide a checksum of each export manifest, and a recommended object-lock policy for long-term retention.

[14:09] Marisol: Great. Let's target the packet + sample by Monday and plan the demo week of 8/25. Thanks everyone.

End of recording.
